header.publisher: Boards of Trustees, Federal HI and SMI Trust Funds / Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services
lawRefs: 2026 Medicare Trustees Report, Tables V.E1 and V.E2 (intermediate estimates for 2027)
CMS fact sheet "Medicare Part D - 2027 National Average Monthly Bid Amount Information" (2026-07-28): base beneficiary premium $41.33
42 U.S.C. 1395r(i) (IRMAA thresholds indexed to CPI-U; top tier frozen through 2027)
header.notes: PROJECTED: as of 2026-11-10 CMS had not yet published the 2027 Parts A & B premiums/deductibles/IRMAA fact sheet (the newsroom was checked; the 2026 one came out 2025-11-14). Part B premium/deductible and Part A premiums/deductible are the 2026 Trustees Report intermediate estimates. FINAL already: Part D base beneficiary premium ($41.33), Part D deductible ($700) and out-of-pocket threshold ($2,400), and therefore the Part D IRMAA surcharges (statutory formula on $41.33). IRMAA thresholds are computed with the statutory CPI-U formula (average of Sep 2025-Aug 2026 over Sep 2017-Aug 2018, rounded to $1,000; joint = 2 x single; MFS upper = $500,000 - lower), which reproduces every published 2020-2026 table. Replace this file when CMS publishes. The `defaults` block is NOT law: it holds editable planning estimates (benchmarks) that the user can override. IRMAA `magiOver` semantics: the top tier legally starts AT the threshold ("greater than or equal to" $500,000 / $750,000; MFS second tier ends "less than" its upper bound), all other tiers start ABOVE it. Premiums are dollars and cents. sha256 is of the raw source document as downloaded.

flags.irmaa.*.magiOver: projected from CPI-U. BLS published no October 2025 CPI-U (shutdown); it was interpolated here. Averaging the 11 published months instead moves the 2nd-4th single thresholds to $142,000 / $177,000 / $212,000 (joint x2, MFS unchanged); the first threshold ($112,000 / $224,000) is the same either way
flags.irmaa.*.partBMonthly: projected: Trustees premium x 1.4 / 2.0 / 2.6 / 3.2 / 3.4, rounded to $0.10 (CMS rounding can differ by $0.10)
